newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks make solid gains, dollar higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks make solid gains, dollar higher.

text.p: European share markets scored solid gains on Tuesday, recovering much of their recent losses after Wall Street extended Monday's rebound from its sharp plunge at the end of last week.

London, Europe's leading stock trading centre, ended up around 1.6 percent and the Paris bourse rose 2.3 percent, while German shares pushed their advance in post-bourse electronic trade to almost 2.7 percent.

But market operators, while not expecting meetings of U.S. and German monetary policy makers this week to raise interest rates just yet, were on the lookout for clues when the next rate move might occur.

"The markets are going to be somewhat on the defensive usually until we hear from the FOMC, though nobody expects them to raise rates," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments in New York.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy arm of the U.S. Federal Reserve, was meeting on Tuesday and its decision on interest rates was expected at about 1815 GMT.
U.S. economists forecast no change in rates for now as recent data suggest growth is moderate and inflation steady.

On the currency market the dollar gained ground after the Bundesbank kept the main German money market rate, the repo, at 3.00 percent and quashed speculation on an imminent interest rate rise by announcing a sharp slowdown in M3 money supply growth, its key policy guide.
"This is very nice for the Bundesbank because it means they can hold off on an interest rate move for the time being," said Gerhard Grebe, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt.
"They can have a relaxed Bundesbank meeting on Thursday," he said, referring to the first meeting of the German central bank's council after its summer break.
The International Monetary Fund and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development also cautioned against higher German rates.
London's FTSE 100 index of blue chips, which had tumbled 2.5 percent on Friday and slipped another 0.6 percent on Monday, ended 1.64 percent higher, snapping a four-day losing streak.
Hopes that U.S. and German interest rates will hold steady encouraged institutional investors to return to blue chip issues, dealers said.
Sharing the positive mood in London, German stocks advanced strongly, aided by Wall Street's revival and a stronger dollar -- good news for German exporters.
The DAX index rose 2.23 percent in floor trade, while the IBIS DAX gained 2.69 percent in computerised business.
"Volumes are pretty thin at the moment but I reckon that when they do come in to the market, they will be on the buy side," one Frankfurt broker said.
The Paris bourse also added 2.3 percent in value as confidence returned, while Amsterdam, a star performer on Monday, pushed more than three percent higher.
European dealers were, however, cautious, pondering whether Friday's widespread drop in stock markets marked an end to a relentless rise or just a short-term correction.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 70 points or 0.9 percent around 7,873 as European markets closed on Tuesday. It had closed up 108.70 points (1.41 percent) at 7,803.36 on Monday, reclaiming a chunk of the 247.37 points it lost on Friday in its second biggest points fall ever.
The Dow, a key influence on markets elsewhere, is around five percent below a record close of 8,259.31 on August 6. But it is 3,200 points or almost 70 percent above its level two years ago.
Asian markets were in a more sombre mood on Tuesday with Tokyo's Nikkei average falling 88.10 points or 0.42 percent to 18,961.0.

Hong Kong, jolted by signs that speculators will attack its dollar after successful assaults on several southeast Asian currencies, suffered even more. The Hang Seng index closed down 3.85 percent at 15,477.26 points.

Financial markets had expected the Bundesbank's repo rate to be held steady for the moment but speculation that German interest rates will soon head higher in a move to curb inflation and underpin the mark has grown.

The dollar hit a high above 1.84 marks after the Bundesbank said July M3 grew an annualised 5.7 percent from the fourth 1996 quarter, below 6.4 percent in June. Economists had expected money supply to grow 6.3 percent.
"The M3 figures take any pressure away from the Bundesbank to raise German rates soon and, as a consequence, the mark should soften," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
The U.S. currency, meanwhile, topped 118 yen in line with its gains against the mark.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 1.8412 marks and 118.34 yen, up from 1.8245 and 117.77 on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index closed up 79.2 points or 1.64 percent at 4,914.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended floor trade up 91.02 points, 2.23 percent, at 4,169.62. The IBIS index for electronic trade finished 109.90 points, or 2.69 percent, higher at 4,190.45.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index closed 66.03 points or 2.3 percent ahead at 2,936.16.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended London trading around $323.25 an ounce, unchanged on balance from Monday. Silver was up two cents at $4.54.
